ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2008 for all applicants and ultimate beneficial owners; enhanced due diligence on politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates; obligatory screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK Sanctions List as extended to Bermuda, HM Treasury/OFSI designations, Bermuda Financial Intelligence Agency (FIA) advisories, OFAC SDN list as best-practice for USD clearing banks, and FATF jurisdictional risk indicators. For this ISIC 3040 defense hardware scope, additional end-user and end-use verification is required, with suspicious activity reports (SARs) filed to the Bermuda FIA where diversion risk is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies - Companies Registry e-Services portal (https://roc.gov.bm); corporate name search and reservation via the online registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be in the Latin alphabet using the English form or an approved transliteration. Non-English names require a certified English translation and a verified transliteration without diacritics. Exempted company names must end with 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation with Registrar consent, and must not be misleadingly similar to an existing registered name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Limited (permitted only as a suffix with Registrar consent for exempted companies)
Royal, Imperial, Crown, Government, Authority, Ministry

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed name under section 13 of the Companies Act 1981, the applicant may: (a) file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies within 14 calendar days, attaching any ministerial consents, trade license evidence, or revised name options; (b) if reconsideration is refused, submit a fresh name reservation application with the applicable fee reflecting the Registrar's objections; and (c) challenge a final administrative refusal by way of judicial review before the Supreme Court of Bermuda, ordinarily filed within 21 days of the final decision. Reserved names lapse after 30 days and may be re-reserved in successive reservation periods.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible for the statutory registered office of a Bermuda exempted company; a physical street address in Bermuda must be maintained through a licensed Corporate Service Provider. Virtual business facilities may be used for offshore sales and marketing activities, but they do not satisfy economic substance requirements under the Economic Substance (Companies and Partnerships) Act 2018.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 25% within the first fiscal year, rising to 35% where Bermuda tax residence or economic substance is claimed for the ISIC 3040 manufacturing scope; below 10% for a purely passive holding vehicle that does not claim economic substance in Bermuda.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Bermuda Companies Act 1981 (as amended), ss. 4(1), 5, 14(1), 15, 18, 24, 42-46, 55(2), 58, 91-92A, 98 and 108; Business Licensing Act 1999; Economic Substance Act 2018 (as amended); Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2018; Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2008. Bermuda is a self-governing British Overseas Territory; UK international obligations, including UN/EU-consolidated arms embargoes and OECD/EU substance standards, are implemented locally.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Registry General, Government Administration Building, 30 Parliament Street, Hamilton HM 12, Bermuda (operating within the Ministry of Economic Development and Labour)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association of an Exempted Company, together with Form E1 (Application for Registration as an Exempted Company), subscriber declarations and a Declaration of Compliance; the formation is perfected by the Registrar's issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation under the Great Seal of Bermuda
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: USD 12,000 minimum issued share capital (Companies Act 1981, s. 14(1)(e)); the capital is stated in the Memorandum and the shares must be subscribed and issued before or at incorporation. No escrow, bank reference or paid-up deposit is lodged with the Registrar; consideration may be cash or non-cash assets. Foreign-currency capital is translated at the prevailing rate of exchange and the company remains free of local currency controls.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-Forma Resolutions of the Subscribers and First Board of Directors. RESOLVED that the subscribers subscribe for and take 12,000 ordinary shares at US$1.00 each, constituting the minimum issued share capital under section 14(1)(e) of the Companies Act 1981, and that the Treasurer issue share certificates upon payment. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at the premises of its licensed corporate-services provider, Hamilton, Bermuda, and be continuously maintained. FURTHER RESOLVED that the persons named in the register of directors be appointed as the first directors and the Secretary, each to serve until the first annual general meeting. FURTHER RESOLVED that the directors endorse all incorporation filings and authorize payment of the statutory fees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance of Bermuda / Office of the Tax Commissioner (OTC) — operational portal: BerGov (www.gov.bm) and the Bermuda Customs e-Declarations module for trade taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Not applicable as Bermuda imposes no VAT, income tax, or turnover tax requiring a general TIN. A foreign-owned Bermuda Exempted Company incorporates under the Companies Act 1981 with the Registrar of Companies and obtains a Bermuda Company Registration Number, which serves as the universal tax identifier for any administrative filings. If the company later becomes subject to Economic Substance filings, the Corporate Income Tax (Pillar Two) regime for in-scope multinational groups, or payroll tax registration, it must additionally register via the OTC's secure online portal using the same Bermuda Company Registration Number. No VAT/TIN certificate is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Bermuda Exempted Company may file a statutory election under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, guaranteeing exemption from all future Bermuda taxes (other than payroll tax, land tax, and customs duties) until 2035. It may also elect to be treated as non-resident for Exchange Control Act 1972 purposes, conditioning its permitted business activities. In addition, an in-scope multinational group may file a corporate income tax status election under the Corporate Income Tax Act 2024 for Pillar Two safe harbour purposes. Bermuda law does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST; Bermuda levies selectively applied customs import duties, stamp duties, payroll tax, and land tax only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A — no VAT/GST registration threshold exists. Importers of commercial goods must obtain a customs identification number and relevant import licences under the Customs Tariff Act 1968; employers are required to register with the Office of the Tax Commissioner for payroll tax when annual local payroll exceeds BMD 25,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, GDPR-style tax clearance, or digital stamping mandate exists in Bermuda. Customs entry documentation for import/export of goods is submitted electronically through the Bermuda Customs e-Declarations portal; the filing is used solely for duty assessment and trade statistics and does not operate as a VAT clearance mechanism.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable because there is no Bermuda VAT/GST to zero-rate. Exports of tangible goods from Bermuda, including all-terrain military tactical vehicles, are entirely outside the scope of Bermuda indirect taxation. Where import duty was paid on goods or components subsequently exported, the Exempted Company may claim a duty drawback under the Customs Tariff Act 1968 subject to proof of export within 12 months of importation and registration as an approved exporter or manufacturing warehouse.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no VAT zero-rating or VAT clawback mechanism in Bermuda. However, false export declarations for duty-drawback claims attract penalties under the Customs Tariff Act 1968, including forfeiture of goods, a penalty of up to three times the full dutiable value, and retrospective recovery of the drawback with interest if the export proof is not substantiated within the 12-month statutory period. Military tactical vehicle exports also require a UK-controlled export licence under applicable Sanctions and Export Control instruments; undertaking or facilitating an unlicensed re-supply triggers UK and Bermuda enforcement action, including unlimited fines, imprisonment, suspension or revocation of the Exempted Company's statutory tax exemption, and remedial clawback of any customs duty relief granted.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) — Bermuda central bank, currency authority and consolidated financial services regulator; HM Treasury and Bank of England as sovereign parent-state authorities; UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) for asset-freeze and arms-embargo administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bermuda dollar (BMD) is legally pegged to the US dollar at 1:1; current-account convertibility is unrestricted for a non-resident-designated Exempted Company. Bermuda levies no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or withholding tax on dividends, interest or royalties, hence profit remittance is effected through an ordinary board-approved dividend or management-fee payment, subject only to Bermuda Companies Act solvency certification and CRS/FATCA reporting. Capital-account transactions are governed by the Exchange Control Act 1972, under which the BMA grants non-resident designation and issues General Consent; once designated, share allotments, capital subscriptions and liquidation proceeds may move freely in any major currency through an authorized dealer, being the operating bank. Material hurdles to convertibility are therefore not Bermudian but extraterritorial: OFAC/OFSI sanctions screening of the ultimate military end-user, EU/UK arms embargoes, and correspondent-bank denial risk for defense-related USD clearing via CHIPS/Fedwire.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Bermuda imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; receivables contracted in USD, GBP, EUR or CNY may remain freely held in foreign-currency accounts without conversion. The applicable regulatory gates are authorization-based: exports of all-terrain military tactical vehicles and controlled components by the group must be covered by a UK export licence under the Export Control Act 2002 and Export Control Order 2008 as extended to Bermuda by Order in Council, or by the export-control authorization of the country of beneficial manufacture; settlement must be supported by invoice, packing list, transport document and end-user certificate, and cleared through the authorized bank's sanctions-screening engine before credit is released.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low-Medium as a supplementary rail only. Bermuda does not maintain a dedicated e-money institution (EMI) licence class; digital payment providers require authorisation under the Banks and Deposit Companies Act 1991 or the Digital Asset Business Act 2018, neither of which is designed for ordinary cross-border corporate treasury settlement. Offshore EMIs (UK FCA-authorised e-money institutions or EU passported EMI/PSP entities) generally exclude merchant category ISIC 3040 / NAICS 336992, being defense tactical hardware, in their acceptable-use policies; onboarding would trigger immediate reputational review and high account-freeze risk. A pragmatic structure is to restrict EMI usage to governed-office expense disbursements and payroll in low-risk corridors, while directing all defense-export receipts exclusively through tier-1 correspondent-connected commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandated for this risk tier. Bermuda AML/ATF Regulations 2018 made under the Proceeds of Crime Amendment Act 2018, together with institutional FATF-compliant policies, require at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner, or an authorized signatory holding power of attorney for a licensed fiduciary, to attend an in-person onboarding interview at the bank's Hamilton office or, exceptionally, before a designated correspondent bank officer for remote-status clients. Pure video/remote account opening is not viable for a High_Risk_Special_License ISIC 3040 vehicle without a pre-existing private-banking relationship with the UBO. Butterfield and HSBC Bermuda additionally require a quorate board meeting resolution approving the account mandate and naming the compliance-designated officer prior to account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening hits linked to the military-defense UBO or directors, or prior association with conflict-zone procurement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party sanctions-screening certificate showing negative OFAC/OFSI/UN/EU hits; passport and residence certification for every director and UBO; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations certified by a licensed Bermuda attorney; full corporate organigram to the ultimate natural persons as filed in the Bermuda beneficial-ownership register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sectoral high-risk classification: manufacture and sale of armored all-terrain military tactical vehicles (ISIC 3040, NAICS 336992) treated as weapons-of-war exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and Certificate of Exemption under the Exempted Companies Act 1981; Bermudian Economic Substance Declaration filing; constitutional documents; manufacturing behind the contract evidenced by a tolling or contract-manufacturing agreement with an OECD-located production entity; valid export authorization from the competent licensing authority; government-issued end-user certificate and non-transfer undertaking naming the final sovereign customer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in counterparty chain, including letters of credit drawn on banks in embargoed or higher-risk jurisdictions, or trans-shipment through third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: LC and standby issuance restricted to G10 OECD banks; complete trade-chain contracts with bills of lading and freight invoices; OFAC/FATF jurisdiction risk assessment memorandum; compliance manual containing UN arms embargo, anti-bribery and non-transfer attestations; audit-trail mapping of every disbursement to the underlying military procurement contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Injection of subscribed capital from low-tax or non-regulated jurisdictions without clear commercial substance in Bermuda.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda substance file comprising locally leased premises, resident director appointments, local corporate administrator or registered agent, IFRS audited annual financial statements, and confirmation of the group's CbCR/FATCA/CRS reporting profile; evidence that the capital injection originates from the UBO's regulated bank account; BMA non-resident designation letter and General Consent reference.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital must be injected by SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV from the UBO's regulated banking account to the Bermuda bank via its USD correspondent, typically JPMorgan, BNY Mellon or Citibank New York, using ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI or CAPT and narrative referencing: Share capital contribution for the named Bermuda Exempted Company, non-resident designated account. Funds must arrive after a Board allotment resolution under the Exempted Companies Act 1981, be receipted into a segregated Capital Escrow Account, and be reconciled against the statutory allotment statement delivered to the Registrar of Companies before share certificates are issued. The operating bank, as authorized dealer, holds BMA General Consent to credit non-resident capital; the BMA must be notified where the issue exceeds delegated-dealer thresholds. Wire verification relies on SWIFT gpi UETR tracking and on the correspondent bank's OFAC pre-screening of the remitter and ultimate funder.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements will use four clearing rails: first, single vendor payments under the operable threshold via SWIFT MT103, with USD over CHIPS/Fedwire, EUR via TARGET2, and GBP via CHAPS; second, documentary import and export Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 using MT700/MT707 for shipment-collateralized component purchases and final-vehicle deliveries; third, standby letters of credit via MT760 for performance bonds, advance-payment guarantees and warranty obligations to sovereign ministries of defense; and fourth, MT202 COV for cover payments of non-USD legs. Each message carries the UETR, full structured remitter and beneficiary address, invoice and export-licence references, and the final military end-user name; release of payment is subject to the bank's transaction-monitoring engine confirming no embargoed destination, no sanctioned owner, and matching of the LC documents comprising end-user certificate, air waybill or bill of lading, and packing list. Government_Direct_Wire and Diplomatic_LC are the designated target payment rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (USD/GBP and USD/EUR) booked under a 1992 or 2002 ISDA Master Agreement with a Bermuda-licensed or London G10 bank, with no BMD/USD hedge required because the Bermuda dollar is pegged 1:1 to the US dollar
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or thinly convertible currencies, principally offshore CNH, INR and TRY, cash-settled in US dollars only

Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) for maturity-matched conversion of sovereign defence-contract revenue tranches, collateralized under an ISDA Credit Support Annex, with trade reporting following UK/EU EMIR obligations of the executing bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty and default interest; further non-compliance triggers Registrar’s publication notice, strike-off from the register, and dissolution of the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year end (default calendar-year financial year: by 30 June annually)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory penalty for non-filing up to BD$250,000; continuing failure subjects the information to exchange with foreign tax authorities and may trigger a UK-requested audit or assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (Beneficial Ownership Portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due with and in the same annual validation cycle as the Form 1E return (anniversary + 42 days); also updated within 14 days after any change of beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or file accurate beneficial ownership records is an offence; applicable default fines and penalties not exceeding BD$250,000, plus potential AML/CFT supervisory reporting to the Bermuda Monetary Authority

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under section 86 of the Companies Act 1981, every exempted company is required to appoint a qualified auditor, subject to a valid exemption by unanimous shareholder resolution that no auditor be appointed; audit is mandatory without exemption for companies whose main business is regulated (insurance, banking, fund administration), issuers listed on the Bermuda Stock Exchange, and entities that fail to secure shareholder exemption. This military-tactical-vehicle manufacturing entity will ordinarily require a statutory audit if it seeks or holds a license that imposes periodic audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda does not issue a national GAAP; applicable standards are International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB or, with auditor acceptance, generally accepted accounting principles of the United States (US GAAP); a single framework must be applied consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must identify and register its beneficial owners (individuals or qualifying holding chains) and maintain a confidential register of beneficial ownership at the registered office. A confirmation of the accuracy and currency of this register must be made in conjunction with the annual validation filing; every share transfer during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the beneficial ownership confirmation filed with the Registrar. The exemption is only available for securities issuers listed on a recognized exchange and their direct subsidiaries, or collective investment schemes in certain cases.

Register of Directors and, where maintained, Register of Officers
Register of Contracts with Directors (if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 4,500 – USD 12,500 per year for registered office, resident representative, and corporate secretarial services; service provider rates vary with AML compliance and UBO record-keeping.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 – USD 35,000 for a certified audit of a private exempted company, depending on scope and whether defense-trade controls or a US/foreign parent audit package applies.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% under the traditional Bermuda Exempted Company regime; 15% for qualifying multinational groups subject to the Bermuda Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 (OECD Pillar Two GloBE implementation), with no branch profit tax or capital gains tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays, deductions, or preferential CIT incentives; ordinary exempted companies pay an annual Government fee (exemption fee) and are subject to payroll tax and stamp duty, but not to tax on income or capital; in-scope CIT groups may compute effective top-up tax using GloBE standard effective tax rate rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return (Form AR) under Bermuda Companies Act 1981; electronic filing via Bermuda Registrar of Companies eServices / Companies eReturn portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the anniversary date of incorporation, unless extended administratively; or within the date fixed by the Registrar for exempted companies with financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, exempted company number, registered office address, date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact registered name and number; use the licensed registered office address in Bermuda; non-resident foreign participation does not alter filing duty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name, nationality, residential address, and date of appointment for each director and officer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors may be listed; a valid local registered office must be maintained and company records physically available in Bermuda.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized and issued share capital, classes of shares, shareholder names and shareholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bermuda law permits 100% non-resident ownership; no minimum paid-up capital is required; record all nominee or beneficial owner details accurately for beneficial ownership filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs daily penalty of BMD 60 up to a statutory maximum of BMD 3,000, discretionary compounding penalties, and possible administrative dissolution/striking-off; false statements may lead to separate monetary penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form CIT-1) filed electronically through the Bermuda Tax Commissioner / Office of Corporate Income Tax e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with estimated quarterly payments for in-scope groups)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For in-scope entities under the Bermuda CIT Act 2023, the annual CIT return is due within six months after the fiscal year-end; estimated tax payments are due on the 15th day of the fourth, sixth, ninth, and twelfth months of the fiscal year (as prescribed by CIT regulations).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before tax from certified financial statements prepared under GAPP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned exempted companies must disclose all global income attributable to Bermuda and adjust for GloBE excluded items if the group is in CIT scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - Covered Taxes and GloBE Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current and deferred taxes attributable to Bermuda, plus substance-based carve-out and tax base adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must ensure the file includes a valid GloBE Information Return annex and reflects any applicable qualified published IFE rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed taxable income after utilization of loss carryforwards and exempting adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward data (max five years under current CIT guidelines) and ownership continuity tests must be documented and preserved.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of up to 10% of the tax ultimately due plus daily accrual (BMD 50 per day up to BMD 5,000); understatement penalties up to 50% of the additional tax; failure to submit GloBE information return may trigger MNE directive sanctions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Bermuda does not impose dividend withholding tax; an exempted company may declare and pay dividends to non-resident shareholders without Bermuda withholding or exchange controls, subject to solvency and sanctioned jurisdiction checks.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Although no Bermuda withholding arises, non-residents may need a Bermuda Certificate of Tax Residence / Certificate of Status issued by the Bermuda Tax Commissioner to claim benefits under the limited US-Bermuda Tax Convention or foreign tax credit in their home jurisdiction. Protocol: submit Form CIT-? (TRC application) with the Registrar/Tax Commissioner, confirm residency and economic substance in Bermuda, then present the TRC together with source-country relief form (e.g., IRS Form W-8BEN-E) at the time of payment. No in-country WHT refund procedure is necessary from the Bermuda side because no tax is withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Bermuda rates: 0% for interest and 0% for royalties paid by an exempted company, including to non-residents. Where the payer or recipient is in a treaty partner state, the US-Bermuda Convention or applicable bilateral agreement may reduce or exempt source-state withholding; absent treaty, the non-resident recipient is subject only to its home-country taxation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory transfer pricing documentation applies to a purely tax-exempt Bermuda exempted company. For in-scope CIT multinational groups, the Bermuda Tax Commissioner requires contemporaneous Master File and Local File where consolidated group revenue is EUR 750 million or more; Local File is triggered for intercompany transactions exceeding BMD 1,000,000 (or equivalent) in aggregate, determined under OECD-compliant Bermuda CIT guidance. Defense procurement contracts with state buyers should be priced commercially and documented even if below the threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Bermuda Economic Substance Amendment (2019) and Economic Substance Regulations apply to resident entities carrying on specified 'relevant activities' (banking, insurance, fund management, financing/leasing, headquarters, shipping, distribution, and intellectual property/service business). Manufacture of armored security transport vehicles under ISIC 3040 is not a designated relevant activity; however, a CIT-resident or treaty-claiming entity must demonstrate full management and control from Bermuda, maintain adequate physical presence and payroll, and conduct core income-generating activities in Bermuda to avoid substance regulatory penalties. Defense manufacturing operations may nevertheless be subject to licensing and end-use audits by the financial action task force competent authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the zero-rate Bermuda entity to conceal the effective ownership of military defense technology, artificially shifting profits from defense contracts, or creating fictitious board minute records without actual management and control in Bermuda.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disgorgement of all profits derived from the sham structure; financial penalties up to BMD 1,000,000 under the Revenue (Tax Information Exchange) provisions and the Criminal Justice (Proceeds of Crime) Act; deregistration of the exempted company; automatic referral to the Bermuda Police Financial Crime Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable for fraudulent involvement: civil restitution of diverted profits, travel ban pending criminal investigation, and imprisonment up to seven years for tax or proceeds-of-crime offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Export Control / Defense Trade Sanction Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Negotiating, brokering, or delivering all-terrain military tactical vehicles to prohibited end-users without obtaining an export license / End-User Certificate from the Bermuda Department of Industry and Labour or relevant UK/Sanctions controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed arms brokering is subject to the Bermuda Arms and Ammunition (Prohibited) legislation: custodial sentence up to seven years and an unlimited fine; corporate license revocation; seizure of the vehicles and proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual board members knowingly engaging can be imprisoned up to seven years, disqualified from corporate management, and held jointly/severally liable to pay contractual compensation to the affected state buyer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify and disclose the natural persons who ultimately control or benefit from the exempted company, masking politically exposed persons, or accepting wire and government diplomatic LC payments without enhanced due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Bermuda proceeds of crime and anti-money laundering penalties reach BMD 100,000 per contravention, plus registration suspension; failure to file beneficial ownership particulars triggers civil penalties and remedial strike-off; banking channels are closed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally fined up to BMD 100,000, barred by the Supreme Court from acting as managers, and, in money laundering cases, imprisoned for up to five years; funds and assets are subject to freezing orders and forfeiture.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pure mailbox entity: no Bermudian payroll, no physical office, no board meetings in Bermuda, while claiming tax-exempt status or treaty residence for active manufacturing and sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Economic Substance Amendment, the Registrar may impose an initial penalty of BMD 10,000, escalating to BMD 500,000 for continued non-compliance, and may strike the entity off the register or initiate tax residence revocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who attest false economic substance declarations commit an offence punishable by imprisonment up to two years; civil recovery powers allow liquidation proceedings against the entity with director disqualification for up to five years.
